prompt: A class has $30$ students. $40\%$ are girls. How many girls?
hint: "$40\%$ are girls" means $40\%$ **of** the $30$ students. In percent problems the word "of" tells you to multiply.

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Find an easier percent first: how many students make up $10\%$ of the class? Then build $40\%$ from that.
"$40\%$ are girls" means $40\%$ **of** the $30$ students. In percent problems the word "of" tells you to multiply.
$10\%$ of $30$ is $3$ students. Since $40\%$ is four times $10\%$, multiply that $3$ by $4$.
$3 \times 4 = 12$, so there are $12$ girls in the class.

explanation: Find $10\%$ of the class first, since it is the total divided by $10$: $30 \div 10 = 3$.
$40\%$ is $4$ groups of $10\%$, so multiply the $10\%$ amount by $4$: $4 \times 3 = 12$.
The decimal method gives the same result: $0.40 \times 30 = 12$.
There are $12$ girls in the class.
